problem: Adapting a general multimodal LLM to continuous VLN needs visual-language alignment, compact temporal inputs, action-space grounding and a stable training stack on non-NVIDIA hardware (Ascend NPUs); prior work does not cover a Pangu-based system.
motivation: A 7B-scale MLLM must be trained efficiently on Ascend 910B NPUs, where unsupported or unstable FP16 operations require selective FP32. The report documents a full pipeline from alignment to offline action prediction and is candid about what offline metrics can and cannot show.
key_idea: Build a two-stage OpenPangu-7B navigator: align EVA-ViT-G with the LLM via a Q-Former and MLP projector on COCO/VG, then use LoRA and structural tokens to adapt it to expert trajectories with five-frame windows and reasoning-then-action output.
insight: Between V5/V6 and V8/V9, NAM rises from about 23-25% to about 62% and NER reaches 100%, but reasoning-then-action output, identity prompting, temporal sampling and action-aware sampling were introduced together. The paper states the causal contribution of each is not isolated, so it is not an ablation. Metrics are teacher-forced and open-loop, so they show only local action agreement, not navigation success.
method: PGMM alignment (Stage 1): frozen EVA-ViT-G/14 and frozen OpenPangu-7B; trains a Q-Former (32 queries) and a two-layer MLP projector (768 to 4096) on COCO and Visual Genome image-caption pairs
Temporal window input: five observations (four history plus current) at stride s, with three learned structural tokens marking image start, image end and frame boundary
Reasoning-then-action output: the model generates reasoning text, then a canonical action from {forward, left, right, stop} (forward 0.25 m, turn 15°)
Stage 2 adaptation: aligned visual pathway and base LLM frozen; only the three structural-token embeddings and LoRA adapters are trained on expert trajectories
Temporal and action-aware sampling: start index e mod s, curriculum (s,p) = (4,0.1), (6,0.6), (8,0.2), where p is the probability of replacing a forward-dominated sample with a turn or stop sample
Data: expert-only collection (beta=1, DAgger-compatible but effectively behavior cloning), 19,699 trajectories and 1,567,487 frames
Ascend training stack: 8 Ascend 910B NPUs, mixed precision, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, selective FP32 for FP16 attention-mask overflow

setting.backbone: OpenPangu-7B (LoRA fine-tuned) + EVA-ViT-G/14 (frozen) + Q-Former and MLP projector (trained)
setting.training_data: Stage 1: COCO and Visual Genome image-caption pairs; Stage 2: 19,699 expert Habitat navigation trajectories (1,567,487 frames) with instructions and expert actions
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m / left 15° / right 15° / stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (trajectory collection only; evaluation is offline, not executed)
setting.privileged: Teacher-forced evaluation supplies expert observation histories; no closed-loop execution

numbers.bench: other:Offline expert-trajectory action alignment (500 held-out trajectories)
numbers.eval_set_note: 500 held-out expert trajectories, teacher-forced open-loop, stride s=1
numbers.extra: Teacher-forced, not closed-loop; EM is 0 because the output includes reasoning text
numbers.evidence: Table 1, row V9: Strict 0.00, Fuzzy 62.29, Non-blank 100.00

numbers.bench: other:Offline expert-trajectory action alignment (500 held-out trajectories)

numbers_note: No standard VLN benchmark numbers (SR, SPL, NE, nDTW) are reported; only offline action-matching metrics. The paper says V3 interval counts sum to 56 rather than 500. Earlier versions V3, V5 and V6 are omitted here.
results: V9 reaches 62.29% NAM and 100% NER (V8: 62.13% NAM) under teacher-forced open-loop evaluation on 500 held-out trajectories, up from V6 at 23.18% NAM and V5 at 25.40%. No comparison with published VLN systems is made, and the results are not closed-loop navigation success.
limitations: Only teacher-forced open-loop action matching is evaluated; there is no SR, SPL, NE or closed-loop simulation, and error accumulation is unmeasured
Version changes are confounded (reasoning format, prompting, sampling all changed together), so no ablation and no causal attribution
Data is expert-only (beta=1), so it is behavior cloning without on-policy correction; per-action logs exist only for V6 and there are no baselines
